newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly up on Monday with new domestic A share issues in both the Shanghai and Shenzhen stock markets absorbing cash from the repo market, traders said.

The annual rate for the most active three-day contract rocketed to 29.90 percent from 6.93 percent last Friday. Traders said institutions bought the three-day contract for the purchase of upcoming new A share issues.
Total turnover rose to 11.65 million lots from 7.66 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said news that state banks were prohibited by the central bank from trading on the repo and spot secondary markets was another important reason for today's rises.

"The ban will move large amount of money supply from the market because the state banks used to be major traders on the repo market," one trader said. "With supply expected to reduce, the rates are expected to continue to stay at high levels."
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai closed mostly down on a liquidity outflow with the repo market attracting a lot of funds, traders said.
The news that state banks were banned from trading on the spot secondary market also dampened sentiment, they said.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006, the market barometer, fell to 114.20 yuan from 114.75 yuan.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market shrank to 675,389 lots from 966,500 lots last Friday.
"Some big institutions sold today in order to trade on the repo market due to the high rates there," said one trader.
"The withdrawal of state banks from the spot market will reduce liquidity," said a second trader. "The spot contracts are expected to continue to be weak in the near term."
